# A — Scaffold, tooling, verify script

**Specs:** `storefront-project-bootstrap` (scenarios "Clean clone to running storefront" and "Framework version below the gate"; the env, secret-bundle and health scenarios are built in E; the deploy part is Y)
**Depends on:** — · **Unblocks:** B, C, D, E (generated by verify-plan) · **Decisions:** D-002, D-003, D-004, D-059
**Owner prerequisites:** none · **Skill refs:** `/commercetools:nextjs-setup-project` command text (source of the create-next-app flags, dependency majors and Tailwind v4 setup); `commercetools-storefront` (Next.js stack adapter)

## Goal
A `site/` Next.js 16 app that installs from a clean clone with `npm ci`, starts with `npm run dev`, and has one command, `npm run verify`, that proves it builds, lints, typechecks and passes its tests. Later workstreams append their own checks to `verify` at the positions fixed below.

## Design

### Repository layout (D-002)
```
b2c-telecom/            (git root)
  .nvmrc                (A-01)  contents: 22
  .gitignore            (A-01)
  site/                 (A-02)  the storefront; every npm command runs here
  openspec/  design/  plan/     (exist; do not touch)
```
`netlify.toml` is created by Y, not here. No `vercel.json` (D-002: Netlify only; the open question in the spec is answered by D-002).

### Scaffold command (A-02)
Run from the repo root. Source: `/commercetools:nextjs-setup-project` step 1, plus non-interactive flags:
```bash
npx create-next-app@^16 site --typescript --app --src-dir=false --tailwind=false --eslint --import-alias "@/*" --use-npm --disable-git --yes
```
If `--tailwind=false` is rejected, use `--no-tailwind`. Afterwards `site/tailwind.config.*` must not exist and `site/package.json` must not list `tailwindcss` (we add v4 ourselves in A-03). create-next-app also writes `site/AGENTS.md` and `site/CLAUDE.md` (keep them) and `site/.gitignore` (edited in A-08).

### Packages (A-03) — exact install commands
Runtime (one command, run in `site/`):
```bash
npm install @commercetools/platform-sdk@^8.27.0 @commercetools/ts-client@^4.10.0 @commercetools/checkout-browser-sdk@^1.7.5 next-intl@^4.14.9 swr@^2.5.1 jose@^6.2.12 server-only@^0.0.1 lucide-react@^1.52.0 tailwindcss@^4.3.3 @tailwindcss/postcss@^4.3.3 postcss@^8.5.29
```
Dev dependencies:
```bash
npm install -D vitest@^5.0.3 @vitejs/plugin-react@^6.1.2 jsdom@^29.1.1 @testing-library/react@^16.3.3 @testing-library/jest-dom@^7.0.1 @testing-library/user-event@^14.6.7 tsx@^4.23.15 @types/node@^22.20.5
```
Rules: `@commercetools/platform-sdk` stays on major 8 and `@commercetools/ts-client` on major 4 (the skill's pinned majors; the registry's majors 9 and 5 are a separate, explicit change — spec "Constraints"). `next` must resolve to `>=16.0.0 <17`, `next-intl` to `>=4.0.0 <5`. Keep `eslint@^9` and `eslint-config-next` exactly as create-next-app wrote them. `lucide-react` is not in the stack list of `ARCHITECTURE.md`; it is added here because workstream I needs icons (Planner default; reported to the owner).

### `package.json` scripts (A-05) — exact final form for A
```json
{
  "dev": "next dev -p 3000",
  "build": "next build",
  "start": "next start",
  "lint": "eslint .",
  "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
  "test": "vitest run",
  "test:watch": "vitest",
  "check:lockfile": "node scripts/check-lockfile.mjs",
  "check:versions": "node scripts/check-versions.mjs",
  "verify": "npm run check:lockfile && npm run check:versions && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build"
}
```
plus `"engines": { "node": ">=22" }`.

### Canonical `verify` order (binding for all workstreams)
Each later workstream inserts its step at the stated position and adds the npm script; it never reorders others.
| # | Step | Added by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `npm run check:secrets` | E |
| 2 | `npm run check:lockfile` | A |
| 3 | `npm run check:versions` | A |
| 4 | `npm run check:tokens` | C |
| 5 | `npm run check:boundaries` | B |
| 6 | `npm run lint` | A |
| 7 | `npm run typecheck` | A |
| 8 | `npm test` | A |
| 9 | `npm run build` | A |
| 10 | `npm run check:bundle` | E |
| 11 | `npm run check:dev-routes` | E |
A's test `test/verify-script.test.ts` encodes this order as a constant array and asserts that the steps present in `package.json` appear in that relative order (so a later workstream that inserts at the wrong place fails its own `verify`).

### Vitest (A-04)
`vitest.config.ts`:
```ts
import path from 'node:path';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  resolve: { alias: { '@': path.resolve(__dirname) } }, // B adds the 'server-only' alias
  test: {
    environment: 'jsdom',
    server: { deps: { inline: ['next-intl'] } }, // next-intl's ESM imports next/navigation without an extension
    globals: true,
    setupFiles: ['./vitest.setup.ts'],
    include: ['**/*.test.{ts,tsx}'],
    exclude: ['node_modules', '.next'],
  },
});
```
`vitest.setup.ts`: `import '@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest'`; `afterEach(cleanup)`; **offline guard** — replace `globalThis.fetch` with a function that throws `Network is disabled in unit tests (fetch <url>); stub fetch or mock the module.` (tests that need fetch use `vi.stubGlobal`). C adds the `next/font/google` mock here; B adds nothing here.
`tsconfig.json`: set `"types": ["vitest/globals", "node"]`, keep `"strict": true`, add `"**/*.mts"` to `include`. Server-only (node) tests start with `// @vitest-environment node`.
`test/utils.tsx` (stub, completed by D, extended by I):
```tsx
import { render, type RenderOptions } from '@testing-library/react';
import type { ReactElement } from 'react';
import { SWRConfig } from 'swr';

export function renderWithProviders(ui: ReactElement, options?: Omit<RenderOptions, 'wrapper'>) {
  return render(<SWRConfig value={{ provider: () => new Map(), dedupingInterval: 0 }}>{ui}</SWRConfig>, options);
}
```

### Version gate (`scripts/check-versions.mjs`, A-07)
Exports `checkVersions(dir: string): string[]` (list of problems; empty = pass). CLI part: `process.cwd()` → print problems to stderr, `process.exit(1)`.
- Resolved version = `package-lock.json` → `packages["node_modules/<name>"].version`; if the lock is missing or lacks the package, fall back to `node_modules/<name>/package.json`. Problem if neither exists: `next: not installed`.
- Required ranges (a constant table in the script): `next` `>=16.0.0 <17.0.0`; `next-intl` `>=4.0.0 <5.0.0`; `@commercetools/platform-sdk` `>=8.0.0 <9.0.0`; `@commercetools/ts-client` `>=4.0.0 <5.0.0`; `tailwindcss` `>=4.0.0 <5.0.0`.
- Message format (exact): `next: resolved 15.5.4, required >=16.0.0 <17.0.0`.
- Extra problems: any file matching `tailwind.config.*` in `dir`; `pnpm`/`yarn` are handled by the lockfile check, not here.
- Tiny semver compare is hand-written (split on `.`, numeric compare, ignore pre-release suffix) — no new dependency.

### Lockfile gate (`scripts/check-lockfile.mjs`, A-06)
Exports `checkLockfiles(dir: string, repoRoot = path.resolve(dir, '..')): string[]`: problem for each of `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lockb` found in `dir` or `repoRoot` (`pnpm-lock.yaml found in <dir>; use npm only`) and `package-lock.json is missing`.

### Environment variables (`site/.env.example`, A-08)
Names per `ARCHITECTURE.md`. Values: non-secrets filled, secrets and OA-02/OA-05 values empty. All server-only; **no** `NEXT_PUBLIC_` anywhere.
```dotenv
# commercetools project spec-test-b2c-telecom (D-001). Copy this file to .env.local; never commit .env.local.
CTP_PROJECT_KEY=spec-test-b2c-telecom
CTP_AUTH_URL=https://auth.us-central1.gcp.commercetools.com
CTP_API_URL=https://api.us-central1.gcp.commercetools.com
# SECRET. Storefront API client created by the owner in Merchant Center (OA-02). Restricted scopes only.
CTP_CLIENT_ID=
# SECRET.
CTP_CLIENT_SECRET=
# Space-separated scopes of that client, each suffixed :spec-test-b2c-telecom (list in plan/TODO-MANUAL-TESTING.md, OA-02).
CTP_SCOPES=
# Checkout application key (OA-05). Empty until the owner has created the Checkout application.
CTP_CHECKOUT_APP_KEY=
# SECRET. At least 32 characters. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 48
SESSION_SECRET=
# Optional. true shows the password reset link on screen under a "demo mode" banner (D-033). Unset = false.
DEMO_SHOW_RESET_LINK=false
# Optional. true uses the built-in deterministic serviceability table (D-020).
SERVICEABILITY_STUB=true
```
Seed-only variables (`CTP_SEED_*`) never appear here; they live in `.env.seed` (F).

### Root `.gitignore` (A-01) and `site/.gitignore` (A-08)
Root `.gitignore` lines: `.envrc`, `.env`, `.env.*`, `!.env.example`, `!.env.seed.example`, `node_modules/`, `.next/`, `coverage/`, `.DS_Store`, `*.tsbuildinfo`, `.netlify/`. In `site/.gitignore` (written by create-next-app, which ignores `.env*`) make sure these two lines exist in this order: `.env*` then `!.env.example` and `!.env.seed.example`. (`.claude/` stays untracked; do not add it.)

### `next.config.ts` (A-09) — narrowed images and dev-only file extensions
```ts
import type { NextConfig } from 'next';

const isProd = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production';

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  // Files named *.dev.ts / *.dev.tsx (route.dev.ts, page.dev.tsx) are routes only in development: production builds do not contain them.
  pageExtensions: isProd ? ['tsx', 'ts', 'jsx', 'js'] : ['tsx', 'ts', 'jsx', 'js', 'dev.tsx', 'dev.ts'],
  images: {
    unoptimized: true, // the commercetools image CDN rejects Next optimiser query parameters
    remotePatterns: [
      { protocol: 'https', hostname: 'images.pexels.com' },
      { protocol: 'https', hostname: 'storage.googleapis.com' }, // commercetools-hosted product images (Planner default)
    ],
  },
};
export default nextConfig;
```
This trick was verified by the planner on Next 16 (2026-10-07): `app/api/health/route.dev.ts` answers in `next dev` and is absent from the `next build` route list. D wraps this config with the next-intl plugin; E adds env validation; neither changes `pageExtensions` or `images`.

### Root files
`app/layout.tsx`: `export default function RootLayout({ children }) { return <html lang="en"><body>{children}</body></html>; }` (D replaces it). `app/page.tsx`: `<main><h1>Bootstrap OK</h1></main>` (D replaces it with the locale redirect). Remove `app/page.module.css`, the Geist font imports (a network fetch at build), `public/*.svg` and `app/favicon.ico` only if they came from the scaffold and are unused (keep `favicon.ico`).

### Pitfalls
- `create-next-app` pulls the newest 16.x: check `npm ls next` shows `16.`, never 15.
- Never run `npm install` with pnpm/yarn in this repo; `check:lockfile` fails the build.
- jsdom has no `fetch` stub by design (offline guard): a test that forgets to stub it fails loudly; that is intended.
- `next build` prints Tailwind/PostCSS errors if `postcss.config.mjs` is wrong: it must be exactly `const config = { plugins: { '@tailwindcss/postcss': {} } }; export default config;` (A-09).
- Do not add `tailwind.config.*`; Tailwind v4 is configured in CSS (C).

## Chrome verification (run by Claude)
- C-A-1: `cd site && npm run dev`, open `http://localhost:3000/` at 1440 px → page shows the heading "Bootstrap OK"; HTTP 200; console has no errors or warnings; network shows only same-origin requests (no fonts.googleapis.com, no external hosts).
- C-A-2: open `http://localhost:3000/does-not-exist` → Next.js default 404 page, document status 404, console clean apart from the 404 resource line.
- C-A-3: `cd site && npm run build && npm run start -- -p 3010`, open `http://localhost:3010/` → "Bootstrap OK"; `view-source` has no `NEXT_PUBLIC_` string; response header `x-powered-by` present is acceptable; console clean.
(After D lands, `/` redirects to `/en-US`; that behaviour is checked in C-D-1, not here.)
